profile.campus: Los Lunas, Valencia County, New Mexico (Meta's Los Lunas data center campus; Data Center Dynamics reported seven buildings on the campus as of 2023, with a further two-building expansion announced)
profile.address: 4250, Messenger Loop Northwest, Meta Los Lunas Data Center, Los Lunas, Valencia County, New Mexico, 87031
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 3 of 5 mapped in this cluster) is part of Meta's Los Lunas campus in Valencia County, New Mexico, south of Albuquerque. Meta broke ground here in 2016 with an initial $250 million building; a third data center opened in 2020, and Data Center Dynamics reported the campus had grown to seven buildings by 2023, with a two-building, roughly $800 million expansion then under construction, expected to take about three years and intended to support both current products and future AI hardware generations. The Village of Los Lunas has approved industrial revenue bonds to assist the build-out through Meta's Greater Kudu LLC affiliate, part of a financing structure the village has used across multiple expansion phases. On power, Meta and Public Service Company of New Mexico (PNM) marked commercial operation of the Route 66 Solar Facility in July 2022, a 49.5-megawatt, 450-plus-acre solar installation in neighboring Cibola County built by NextEra Energy Resources with more than 150,000 bifacial solar modules, built specifically to help supply renewable power to the Los Lunas data center. Meta's own fact sheet reports more than $2.5 billion invested in the New Mexico campus overall, roughly 400 operational jobs once complete, 1,100 peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $4.9 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, LEED Gold certification for campus buildings, and a Meta-supported total of 885 megawatts of new renewable energy plus 100 megawatts of battery storage added in New Mexico as part of Meta's global net-zero and 100%-renewable-electricity commitments. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual Los Lunas structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

reading.body:
Meta's Los Lunas campus in New Mexico has no published power capacity, which means its scale in the AI hardware build-out cannot be assessed against other facilities. The campus exists as a physical presence verified in September 2026, with Meta having invested $2.5 billion and employed 1,100 peak construction workers since groundbreaking in 2016, but Meta does not disclose the megawatts it consumes or the number of buildings on site. Without those figures, the campus cannot be ranked against peers or included in calculations of regional AI compute density.

The state context makes this absence of data more significant. New Mexico has 14 mapped data center facilities but zero published megawatts across all of them, which means no facility operator in the state publishes power consumption to a standard reference source. The Los Lunas campus therefore cannot be placed in a meaningful hierarchy even within New Mexico. Its strategic importance to AI scaling depends entirely on information Meta has chosen not to release.

The campus qualifies for operational sustainability claims. Buildings achieve LEED Gold certification, electricity is matched to 100 percent renewable energy, and Meta reports a supporting project adding 885 megawatts of new renewable energy plus 100 megawatts of battery storage in the state. These certifications speak to the campus's alignment with grid constraints, but they describe energy sourcing and building standards, not AI compute capacity. Without published power figures, this campus remains a major capital commitment with unknown leverage on the binding constraint the site identifies: compute downstream of buildings and power, power downstream of the grid.
